newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland suspends duties for computer components.
newsitem.headline: Poland suspends duties for computer components.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved several regulations which, until the end of 1997, suspend duties on a range of computer parts in a bid to help domestic computer hardware firms, a senior official said.

Deputy Economy Minister Maciej Lesny told a news conference after the cabinet meeting the regulations would, among others, reduce to zero from three percent duties on memory, microchips, disk drives and some other components.
The government also decided to introduce duty-free quotas on such products as monitors and keyboards.
"This is an attempt to create a level playing field for Polish computer and electronics makers...Surveys indicate a large reduction in sales," Lesny said.
He said present customs regulations made imports of whole computers cheaper than assembling them from imported components, puting domestic computer firms at a disadvantage.
Lesny added that last year out of 500,000 personal computers sold in Poland 70 percent were made domestically.
He told Reuters after the conference that the government planned to publish the regulations next week and they would come into force two weeks after their announcement.
